title: Any linear key rule on a keyword tableau, with no rule named: order 5 with free coefficients (plus a drift term), text-fed rules with two key taps, and arbitrary tables of the key, plain or cipher letter 1-6 back
k4_result: 0 of 2,209,959,555 exact tests pass (6,669,928 key streams: 666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts x C-P and C+P). By test: A (order 5 + constant, 8 checks) 0, chance predicts 0.00003; A2 (order 5 + drift e*i, 7 checks) 0, chance 0.0008; B (K = a1 K[i-1] + a2 K[i-2] + u P[i-s] + v C[i-t] + c, 324 settings per stream, 7-15 checks) 0, chance 0.082; C1 (K[i] = g(K[i-d]), any table, 7+ forced repeats) 0, chance 0.001; C2 (K[i] = g(P[i-d]) or g(C[i-d]); plain 1 back 10 repeats, plain 2 back 8, cipher 1 back 8, cipher 2 back 7) 0, chance 0.0009. Nothing to decrypt. Gauges below the bar behave as chance says: order 6 at 5 checks 1 pass (chance 0.56; reading gibberish, -8.66 on the big model, and its run from block 1 reproduces only 5 of 11 block-2 key letters); key table at 5-6 repeats 1 (chance 0.61; 3 new letters, nothing to read); text table at 5-6 repeats 0 (chance 0.63). The mod 2 halves pass at the predicted rate (A: 25,722 against 26,054).
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each on A-Z, KRYPTOS and a different third of the alphabets (about 2.22M key streams, 732M exact tests each): 0, 0, 0 pass at 7+ checks in every test. Gauges: 18, 0, 0 (seed 1: 1 order-6 pass and 17 text-table passes at 5-6 repeats against 0.76 predicted; these come in clumps because sister alphabets share the letters involved). Same picture as K4: nothing to read on either side.
planted: 9/9 found and read back with 0 wrong letters (cubic key; three-tap chain key with multipliers; generator a K + c; order 4 with drift; text-fed rule with P 3 back and C 5 back; order 5 with drift; tables of the last key, plain and cipher letter), each on a random dictionary tableau among 16,675 others; 8/8 still found with the second clue moved 2 places (the order-5-with-drift rule needs the carved positions and was not moved)
scope_limits: Only tableaux built from A-Z, KRYPTOS and the dictionary keyword alphabets (plain, ~cols, ~keyed) in the five standard layouts, key read as C-P or C+P, arithmetic mod 26; no hidden alphabet. Pure key rules: order 5 at most (order 6 leaves 5 checks and is only a gauge). A constant that changes with position is covered only as a drift e*i (order 4 with drift at any gap, order 5 with drift at the carved gap); a periodic or keyword-driven constant is not covered. Text-fed rules: at most two key taps (1 and 2 back), one plain and one cipher letter each 1-6 back, numbered on the tableau alphabet, A-Z or KRYPTOS; no rule using the current plain letter, two plain letters, or lags over 6. Table rules: one input only, and only lags with 7+ forced repeats were judged (key letter d back: judged only for streams whose key letters repeat enough, 6.5M stream-lags in all; plain 1-2 back; cipher 1-2 back); lags 3-6 of the text tables have 6 or fewer repeats and are gauge only or unjudged. Rules must hold unbroken inside each clue block; a rule that restarts or skips inside a block is not covered. Controls used a third of the alphabets each; planted texts were searched in a 1-in-40 sample of the alphabets plus the true one. The clue pre-filter gives PASS (score 0.0: it breaks nothing and explains no hint).

negative.family: Key from a linear recurrence or a look-up table (any coefficients) on a keyword tableau
negative.hypothesis: Each K4 key letter is a fixed linear mix of the few key letters before it (optionally plus one earlier plain and one earlier cipher letter), or a fixed table of one earlier key, plain or cipher letter, on a keyword tableau.
negative.scope: 666,993 alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms) x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort = 6,669,928 key streams. Exact solve mod 13 and mod 2 on the 13 + 11 forced key letters with all coefficients free: order 5 + constant (8 checks; contains every lower order, polynomial keys to degree 4, chain addition with any taps to 5 back and any multipliers, a K + c generators, order 4 + drift; independent of the gap between the clues); order 5 + drift e*i (7 checks, carved positions); K[i] = a1 K[i-1] + a2 K[i-2] + u P[i-s] + v C[i-t] + c for s, t = 1..6 and 9 numberings (7-15 checks); arbitrary tables K[i] = g(K[i-d]), g(P[i-d]), g(C[i-d]) where the clues force 7+ repeats.
negative.outcome: Dead: 0 of 2.21 billion exact tests pass on K4 (chance predicts 0.085 in all); nothing to decrypt (controls: 3 shuffled K4s on a third of the alphabets each, 0, 0, 0; planted 9/9 read back with 0 wrong letters, 8/8 still found with the second clue moved 2 places)

follow_ups: The same order-free test with a hidden alphabet: on a fully hidden tableau the key letters are unknown, but for a Quagmire III the order-R recurrence is still polynomial in the 26 unknown positions; only order 1 (K[i] = a K[i-1] + c) keeps the system small enough to enumerate a, c and solve the rest linearly.

A constant driven by a short key word: K[i] = a1 K[i-1] + a2 K[i-2] + w[i mod p]. For p <= 6 this is 2 + p unknowns against 22 equations and can be solved exactly per key stream; it needs the carved gap.
